answer: Proof of Personhood serves as a foundational atlas for verifying unique identity within an agent network. By requiring agents to solve cryptographically anchored challenges at the network inlet, the system ensures that compute power or social trust remains tethered to finite physical entities. An attacker attempting to flood this river of nodes faces prohibitive computational costs, as each fake identity necessitates an expensive, non-transferable stake that scales linearly with the Sybil expansion.
